angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 499,105 km at 113.55 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.8065 +/- 0.0105 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 113.55 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.717414 solar radii from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-929 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract): 499,105 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.7 +/- 0.088 solar masses from Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the mass of TIC 175532955 (VizieR IV/39/tic82); no NASA Exoplanet Archive row gives one, nor does Gaia DR3 FLAME (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ab3467); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4457.16 K from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-929 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-929 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-929.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.572, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-929 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.73994, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
